title: Frontend mid scenario third party script slowdown
topic: Frontend mid scenario third party script slowdown
question: How would you diagnose this, and what options would you consider to fix it without just removing the feature?
idealAnswer:
Confirm the cause first using the performance panel or a tool like WebPageTest/Lighthouse, checking whether the third-party script is blocking the main thread, delaying other resources, or shifting layout after load

Check how and when the script is loaded, a synchronous <script> tag in the head blocks parsing, switching to async or defer (or loading it after the page's own critical content) reduces its impact on initial render

Consider lazy-loading non-critical widgets (like a chat bubble) until after the main content is interactive, or until a user interaction signals intent (e.g. scroll, hover)

Consider using a web worker or a facade/placeholder pattern (showing a lightweight static stand-in that loads the real, heavy widget only on interaction) to defer the actual cost

Check for layout shift caused by the widget injecting itself into the page after load, reserving space for it upfront prevents CLS regressions

Communicate the measured tradeoff back to the stakeholders who requested the script, performance budgets should be a shared, visible constraint, not something engineering absorbs silently
